answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, where each vertex distributes mass only across authenticated edges. An adversarial sybil cluster can mirror internal endorsements, yet if its external cut is sparse, its conductance is low. Spectral expansion and min-cut transitivity then bound walk leakage into the cluster, limiting its aggregate voting weight despite arbitrary internal coordination; a high-conductance terrace of honest attestations remains dominant.
